newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - June 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - June 17.

text.p: THE DOMINION

Push for NZ to host Internet casinos: Internet casinos licensed to operate from websites in New Zealand could earn the government up to $1 billion a year in tax revenue, the Casino Control Authority said on Monday. Page 1.

Sir Tipene signals asset allocation for urban Maoris: Treaty of Waitangi Fisheries Commission chairman Sir Tipene O'Regan signalled on Monday that urban Maori authorities might receive some fisheries assets in a bid to avoid further wrangling over some $300 million in Treaty settlements. Page 2.
Nine candidates under scrutiny: Police are making further inquiries into the general election returns of nine candidates, but are refusing to name them or their parties. Page 2.

ACC rules criticised: The International Labour Organisation has asked New Zealand to change "without further delay" accident compensation rules, estimated to cost workers $23 million a year, that are in breach of the organisation's convention. Page 2.

Coalition caucus may ease strains: Prime Minister Jim Bolger will host a joint National-NZ First meeting tonight, followed by a dinner at Premier House in Wellington, in a bid to patch up strained coalition relations. Page 2.

NZ Post cleared to buy frieght companies: NZ Post has been cleared by the Commerce Commission to buy all but one company in Freightway's express frieght division, but a spokeswoman for the state-owned enterprise said on Monday night that the deal was far from done. Page 13.

Apple Fields blames loss on transition: Apple Fields, the corporate orchardist in the process of becoming a property development company, has blamed its latest half-year loss on the costs of making that transition. Page 13.
Total overseas debt falls $2.8 billion: Total overseas debt fell $2.8 billion or 3.5 percent in three months to the end of March as the government continues to pay off debt. Page 13.
Budget policy on debt tender 'uncertain': The main area of uncertainty for financial markets in the next week's Budget for is the debt tender programme, according to Bankers Trust. Page 13.
THE NEW ZEALAND HERALD
Tot twice lined up for home of abuse: A repeatedly bashed Auckland baby was to be placed in not one but two abusive homes by social welfare staff, health workers revealed on Monday.
Compliance costs will drop -- Luxton: The Minister of Commerce, John Luxton, says business should start to see a reduction in regulatory and compliance costs in the New Year.

Pig power opposes import levy: The pig industry's largest investor, PIC New Zealand, has spoken out strongly against a proposed levy on imported pork meat and the Pork Industry Board's involvement in commercial investments.

Fernz Corp looks to use French assets for agri-chemicals push: Fernz Corp will carve-up French chemicals concern Compagnie Francaise des Produits Industriels if its takeover offer for the company is successful.

PC mag gains market as rival delays: New Zealand's biggest-selling computer monthly, PC World, has been left with a virtual monopoly in the computer magazine market while a deal is struck to reintroduce its main rival, PC Magazine, to the newstands.

Malaysian car investor happy with Colonial: Even though Guinness Peat Group drove off with a $14.5 million profit from a brief foray into Colonial Motor Company, the new Malaysian shareholders are happy with their 33.9 percent investment.
Air NZ food unit sold: Air New Zealand's catering unit is being bought by SC International Services.
THE PRESS

Husband hero of shark attack: Two-hour wait for care: A shark attack on a Christchuch woman in a remote area of Fiji on Sunday brought out the hero in her husband as he fought to save her life. Page 1.
Unity on power issue: The axe hovering over the South Island's power price differential will be high on the agenda when the island's MPs meet on Wednesday at Parliament. Page 3.

Employment reform policy on track -- MP: Employment Minister Peter McCardle on Monday insisted the government's employment reform policy was on track, saying he had never intended full implementation of the strategy before the second half of next year. Page 6.

Abuse-case confession: The Children, Young Persons and their Families Service's (CYPFS) handling of a case in which a six-year-old Auckland girl with gonorrhoea was returned to her abusive home was indefensible, Social Welfare Minister Roger Sowry said on Monday. Page 8.
MP threatened over wild horses: Conservation Minister Nick Smith has been receiving dozens of abusive phone calls and veiled death threats at his Nelson home over the Kaimanawa wild horses. Page 8.

Bunge double-up: 'possession is nine-tenths of the law': Dividend money mistakenly paid to shareholders in Defiance Food Industries legally belongs to the company's new owner, says Eion Edgar, a Dunedin sharebroker. Page 25.
Iddison Group trims loss: Iddison Group Vietnam reported on Monday an after-tax loss of $1.1163 million, compared with $1.207 million in the 1996 year. Page 25.

Tranz Rail, Wisconsin examine Aust possibilities: Tranz Rail and its majority shareholder Wisconsin Central are taking a close look at the books of three operations owned by the Australian National Railways Commission. Page 25.
